title: September 23, 1908: India's "National Poet" was born to a farmer in rural Bihar.

sources.text: ThePrint, 2021 - Ramdhari Singh Dinkar, the 'Rashtrakavi' whose words spoke to every Indian

caption:
September 23, 1908: India's "National Poet" was born to a farmer in rural Bihar.

His father was a farmer; his mother shaped his early discipline and values. He studied history, politics and Sanskrit at Patna University and his fiery nationalist poetry - full of heroic sentiment - earned him the title 'Rashtrakavi,' India's national poet, before independence had even arrived.

Dinkar's epic poem 'Rashmirathi,' retelling the Mahabharata's Karna, remains a landmark of Hindi literature. He won the Sahitya Akademi Award (1959), the Bharatiya Jnanpith (1972) and the Padma Bhushan - and served in the Rajya Sabha from 1952 to 1964, appointed by Nehru himself. Yet Dinkar still recited verses in Parliament criticizing Nehru's own government - respect and independence, at the same time.

A Viksit Bharat by 2047 needs voices that can be honored by power and still hold it accountable. Dinkar proved a farmer's son could become the nation's poetic conscience and never trade his voice for his seat.
